title: Effective strict-henselian descent of a locally finite-type group datum
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $D=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ a chosen strict henselization, $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $F=\operatorname{Frac}D$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-sc-ring-strict-henselization, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $H$ be a smooth separated commutative $D$-group scheme locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; its multiplication, identity and inverse satisfy the commutative group identities, and separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose $H_F$ is of finite type and every finite subset of $|H|$ lies in an affine open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose $H$ has a descent datum $\alpha:p_0^*H\simeq p_1^*H$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_RD)$ satisfying the cocycle on $\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_RD\otimes_RD)$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Assume $\alpha$ respects the multiplication, identity and inverse, and its restriction after inverting a uniformizer of $R$ is the canonical datum of a specified smooth separated finite-type commutative $K$-group $V$ under an identification $H_F\simeq V_F$ [def-pc-base-change]. Then the datum is effective in smooth separated commutative group schemes: there exist a smooth separated commutative $R$-group scheme $G$ and an isomorphism $G_D\simeq H$ inducing $\alpha$ and the specified generic identification $G_K\simeq V$. Neither $H$ nor $G$ is required to be quasi-compact. No Néron mapping property is assumed.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Theorem 1 and Corollary 3 proof, printed pp.157–159 (PDF pp.163–165), and the lft descent invoked in 10.1 Proposition 7 proof, printed p.293 (PDF p.299). Agent formulation of the lft effectivity input with finite-affine-neighbourhood and finite generic-fibre hypotheses explicit; not an assertion that finite-type group descent alone covers a non-quasi-compact group. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. Agent formulation where explicitly indicated.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}D$, and $p:S'\to S$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat], $R\to D$ is faithfully flat. Its map on spectra is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] to the affine charts (equivalently the single full affine chart) to obtain that $p$ is flat. A morphism between affine schemes is affine; hence $p$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Thus $p$ is a flat quasi-compact surjection, with no finite-presentation assertion about $p$.

source.place: Tag 07QM, faithful flatness of strict henselization; algebra.tex Tag 00HP and morphisms.tex affine flatness and affine quasi-compactness.

proof.text: Choose a geometric closed point $\bar s$ of $S$ realizing the residue separable closure used to choose $D$. Apply [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] to the full affine open $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$: since $R$ is local, its localization at the closed point is $R$ itself. This identifies the chosen algebraic $D$ with $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$ as an $R$-algebra, including the structural map, and shows that $D$ is strictly henselian. Thus [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] applies and makes $D$ a DVR and $R\to D$ an injective local map. Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. Its image is nonzero and in the maximal ideal of $D$. By [lem-sc-local-domain-dim-one-principal-localization-fraction-field], $R[1/\pi]=K$ and $D[1/\pi]=F$. Tensor/localization compatibility follows from the universal property of inverting $\pi$: maps out of either side are pairs of agreeing maps with $\pi$ invertible. In particular the generic restriction of the Cech datum is precisely the specified datum over $F/K$.

source.place: Tags 04HX/04GW, the affine-ring comparison; Tag 0AP3, preservation of a DVR; localization universal property.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-trait-special-neutral-finite-type-open] to $H/D$. It gives the open subgroup $U=H\setminus(H_s\setminus H_s^0)$, with the entire generic fibre $U_F=H_F$ and only the special identity component. Crucially $U$ is of finite type, although $H$ need not be. Since $\alpha$ is a group isomorphism, the same lemma makes $U$ stable under $\alpha$ on the full double overlap. Its restricted datum still satisfies the cocycle. Since $D$ is strictly henselian, the set-indexed opens $U_\lambda=\lambda U$, for $\lambda\in H(D)$, cover $H$. Each is a smooth separated finite-type scheme, by its translation isomorphism with $U$.

source.place: (3.2)(d), (3.3.4), and the smooth translate-cover argument following (3.3.3), printed pp.40-42.

proof.text: Now apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-field-trait-descent] to the faithfully flat map of DVRs $R\to D$ and the finite-type group $U$, with its restricted group-compatible datum. Obtain a smooth separated finite-type $R$-group $G_0$ and a datum-compatible group isomorphism $\theta_0:(G_0)_D\simeq U$. All finite-type hypotheses of that theorem hold here. This use of BLR descends the finite-type subgroup, rather than applying its theorem to the whole locally finite-type $H$.

source.place: 6.5 Theorem 1, printed p.157 (PDF p.163); its invariant ample-divisor/quasi-projective proof is used through the existing finite-type descent node.

proof.text: For each $\lambda\in H(D)$, let $v_\lambda\in V(F)$ be its generic point under the specified comparison $\beta:H_F\simeq V_F$. Apply [lem-sfb-strict-local-generic-point-etale-approximation] to obtain an etale local DVR neighbourhood $T_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}A_\lambda\to S$, a faithfully flat local injection $A_\lambda\to D$, and $a_\lambda\in V(\operatorname{Frac}A_\lambda)$ pulling back to $v_\lambda$. Thus $p$ factors as $S'\xrightarrow{q_\lambda}T_\lambda\xrightarrow{r_\lambda}S$; $q_\lambda$ is flat and surjective by the same affine criteria as step 1 and is quasi-compact because it is affine. No claim that the translating points are already $K$-valued is made.

source.place: 10.1 Proposition 7, printed p.293 (PDF p.299), translation construction; generic points become defined over etale local neighbourhoods by the cited approximation lemma.

proof.text:
The two pullbacks of $\lambda$, compared using $\alpha$, agree generically on $B=D\otimes_{A_\lambda}D$: via $\beta$ both are the pullback of $a_\lambda$. They agree everywhere. Indeed $\pi$ is a nonzerodivisor on $D$, and tensoring its multiplication injection with the flat $A_\lambda$-module $D$ keeps it injective on $B$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. As $H$ is separated, pulling back its diagonal by the pair of sections gives a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; thus their equalizer is a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; its ideal $I$ satisfies $I[1/\pi]=0$. Every element of $I$ is killed by a power of $\pi$, so injectivity gives $I=0$. Because $U$ is stable and $\alpha$ respects multiplication, $U_\lambda$ is consequently stable for the datum over $S'/T_\lambda$, and translation gives a compatible isomorphism
$$\theta_\lambda:(G_0)_{A_\lambda}\times_{T_\lambda}S'\xrightarrow{\theta_0}U\xrightarrow{t_\lambda}U_\lambda.$$
The compatibility equation is $\alpha(t_{p_0^*\lambda}(p_0^*u))=t_{p_1^*\lambda}(\alpha(p_0^*u))$, since the two sections have just been proved equal. Thus these finite-type pieces have effective data over the etale neighbourhoods.

source.place: 10.1 Proposition 7 translation/gluing argument, printed p.293; elementary separated-equalizer argument over the pi-torsion-free overlap. No source theorem is used to extend a section across the closed fibre.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-etale-effective-open-chart-descent] with $Y=H$, the covering $\{U_\lambda\}$ of step 3, the factorizations $p=r_\lambda q_\lambda$ of step 5, and the models $Z_\lambda=(G_0)_{A_\lambda}$ and isomorphisms of step 6. It produces an algebraic space $X/S$, an isomorphism $\theta:X_D\simeq H$ inducing $\alpha$, and an etale atlas given by these descended finite-type pieces. Its functor of points is exactly the compatible-section equalizer displayed in that lemma. The extra chart hypotheses are verified before this application; separated locally finite presentation alone is not being treated as an fpqc effectivity criterion.

source.place: Agent effective-open-chart gluing criterion, from Tags 023Q, 02L3, 02VN and bootstrap.tex Tag 04S6; applied only after construction of the effective etale-local charts.

proof.text: For each $T/S$, the compatible sections of step 7 form a subgroup of $H(T\times_S S')$: if $y,z$ are compatible, then $\alpha(m(y,z))=m(\alpha(y),\alpha(z))=m(p_1^*y,p_1^*z)$, with all terms pulled to the double overlap; likewise $\alpha(e)=e$ and $\alpha(i(y))=i(\alpha(y))$. Thus multiplication, identity and inverse restrict to these subsets and commute with every pullback in $T$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space], natural transformations are morphisms of spaces; these operations therefore define $m_X:X\times_S X\to X$, $e_X:S\to X$, and $i_X:X\to X$. Each commutative group identity holds pointwise in the ambient group of sections of $H$, and hence on $X$. The restriction identification in [lem-sfb-etale-effective-open-chart-descent] makes $\theta$ a group isomorphism, since all operations were obtained by restricting those of $H$.

source.place: Tag 023Q compatible-section construction; elementary restriction of group operations to the equalizer.

proof.text: The single map $p$ is an fpqc covering: it is flat, quasi-compact and surjective by step 1. Its pullback of $X\to S$ is the separated locally finite-type morphism $H\to S'$. The separatedness clause of [lem-sfb-space-fpqc-qc-separated-descent] gives that $X\to S$ is separated, and the fpqc-locality clause of [lem-sfb-space-lft-smooth-fpqc-locality] gives that it is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-trait-group-space-schematicity] to this group algebraic space over the given DVR $R$. Choose a representing $S$-scheme $G$. Transport $m_X,e_X,i_X$ along the representing isomorphism; these are scheme morphisms and satisfy the same commutative group identities. We now have a separated locally finite-type commutative $R$-group scheme with $G_D\simeq H$ inducing $\alpha$.

source.place: Raynaud, Specialisation du foncteur de Picard, Publications Mathematiques IHES 38 (1970), Theoreme 3.3.1, printed p.40 (PDF p.15); specialization of the locally Noetherian normal dimension-one base to a DVR. This theorem says locally of finite type, not finite type. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read at https://numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1970__38__27_0.pdf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent] to $G\to S$ and $p:S'\to S$. The latter is flat, quasi-compact and surjective by step 1, and the base change of the former is $H\to S'$, which is smooth by hypothesis. It follows that $G\to S$ is smooth. This application imposes no quasi-compactness on $G$ and no finite presentation on $p$.

source.place: Tag 02VL, smoothness is fpqc local on the base.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pd-morphisms-descend] over $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ to the compatible isomorphism $(G_K)_F\simeq H_F\xrightarrow{\beta}V_F$ of step 2. Both data are effective already, with descended schemes $G_K$ and $V$. This is a legitimate fpqc application: $F/K$ is a nonzero field extension, hence tensoring is exact and faithful (choose a $K$-basis of $F$ containing $1$), and its affine spectrum map is surjective and quasi-compact. Descend the inverse map as well. Uniqueness in the same lemma makes both composites the identity, since this is true after extension to $F$. It likewise shows that the descended isomorphism respects multiplication, identity and inverse: the two maps in each group diagram agree after extension to $F$ and are therefore equal. This gives the required $G_K\simeq V$ with exactly the prescribed base change $\beta$. The effective charts cover all of $H$, so no component has been discarded.
